description: How to work in this repo day-to-day. Covers the build cycle (plan → branch → implement → test → merge), completeness rules (no placeholders, no stub code), testing philosophy (test orchestration, not just leaves), commit discipline, and multi-agent coordination (task scoping, handoff reports, review-before-merge). Read this before writing any code.

Canonical stack and architecture decisions. Defines Rails 8 + SQLite + Tailwind + Stimulus, key gems (active_interaction, discard, audited, view_component), auth approach (magic links), testing tools (RSpec, Capybara), and deployment model (single-server, no external deps). Consult when adding dependencies, choosing patterns, or setting up new features.

The product spec — what the system does. Domain model, use cases (check-in/out, manual entries, reports), allocation algorithm (equal-split with empty-house pooling), constraints, edge cases, screen designs, and roles/permissions. Read when implementing any feature, writing validations, or making UI decisions.

Clickable HTML prototype of all three end-user screens (Dashboard, Consumption Report, Readings History). Static sample data, working navigation, form flows with toast confirmations, FontAwesome icons with classic/duotone toggle. Serve via `python3 -m http.server 8080` from prototype/. Reference this when building UI to match the approved look, layout, and interaction patterns.

One-time bootstrap guide for setting up the project from scratch. Covers spec analysis, stack selection, project scaffolding, CLAUDE.md creation, linting setup, and CI pipeline. Only relevant if the project hasn't been initialized yet — not needed for ongoing development.

Rules for maintaining the specification itself. Defines principles (behavior over implementation, mirror not roadmap, one canonical definition) and the update workflow (spec changes ship with code changes, periodic audits via re-generation). Read when editing the spec or resolving [UNCLEAR] markers.

Policy for building developer automation (scripts, slash commands, git hooks, generators). Defines the Rule of Three (build only after 3 occurrences), naming convention (_agen suffix), budget limits (1 tool per 5 features, max 15 min build time), and documentation requirements. Read when considering building a new tool or checking tool-suggestions.md.

Defines the three team roles (Lead, Developer, QA) and their expected behaviors. Lead: scope guardian, quality gatekeeper, context broadcaster. Developer: transparent about state, integration-aware, explicit handoffs. QA: exploratory testing, evidence-driven (failing tests as bug reports), regression-conscious. Read when coordinating multi-agent work or unclear on handoff expectations.

Deployment infrastructure and known issues. Covers K3s/Flux GitOps pipeline, GHCR image publishing, Tailwind CSS Docker build gotcha (split RUN commands), production bootstrap rake task, environment variables, release process, and resolved deployment issues. Read when deploying, debugging production, or modifying the Dockerfile/CI.

Frontend pitfalls and patterns. Covers flash/toast rendering (full page vs Turbo Stream), HTML5 form validation helper usage, ActiveInteraction vs ActiveRecord error translation, Stimulus target preservation in Turbo replacements, and form styling conventions. Read when working on forms, flash messages, toasts, or Turbo Stream responses.
